passages.text: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Nicodemus was a man.
He belonged to the Pharisees.
He was a leader among the Jews.
His name was Nicodemus.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων Νικόδημος ὄνομα αὐτῷ ἄρχων τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.”
passages.sermon:
Nicodemus was a Pharisee.
He was a leader of the Jews.
Nicodemus came to Jesus at night.
He spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Rabbi, we know you are a teacher from God.
No one can do the signs you do unless God is with him.”
passages.original: οὗτος ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν νυκτὸς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ῥαββί οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ἐλήλυθας διδάσκαλος οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται ταῦτα τὰ σημεῖα ποιεῖν ἃ σὺ ποιεῖς ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nicodemus.
Jesus replied to him.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.”
No one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν οὐ δύναται ἰδεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: “How can a man be born when he is old?” Nicodemus asked. “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?”
passages.sermon:
Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
Nicodemus came to Jesus at night.
Nicodemus spoke to Jesus.
Nicodemus asked a question.
Nicodemus said, “How can a man be born when he is old?”
Nicodemus asked, “Can a man enter his mother’s womb a second time?”
Nicodemus asked, “Can he be born again in this way?”
passages.original: Λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Νικόδημος Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος γεννηθῆναι γέρων ὤν μὴ δύναται εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ δεύτερον εἰσελθεῖν καὶ γεννηθῆναι

passages.text: Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nicodemus.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
No one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.
Only those born of water and the Spirit can enter God’s kingdom.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ Πνεύματος οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
A person can be born in two ways.
One way is by human birth.
Human birth produces human life.
Another way is by the Spirit of God.
The Spirit of God gives spiritual life.
What is born from human parents is human.
What is born from the Spirit is spirit.
passages.original: τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς σάρξ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος πνεῦμά ἐστιν

passages.text: Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nicodemus.
\r\nJesus is the Son of God.
\r\nJesus said, “Do not be amazed.”
\r\nI told you, ‘You must be born again.’
passages.original: μὴ θαυμάσῃς ὅτι εἶπόν σοι Δεῖ ὑμᾶς γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν

passages.text: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nicodemus.
\r\nJesus explained how the Spirit works.
\r\nThe wind blows wherever it wants.
\r\nYou hear the wind’s sound.
\r\nYou do not know where the wind comes from.
\r\nYou do not know where the wind goes.
\r\nEveryone born of the Spirit is like this.
\r\nYou cannot see or control the Spirit’s work.
\r\nYou can notice the effects of the Spirit.
\r\nYou do not fully understand how the Spirit works.
passages.original: τὸ πνεῦμα ὅπου θέλει πνεῖ καὶ τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ἀκούεις ἀλλ’ οὐκ οἶδας πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει οὕτως ἐστὶν πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος

passages.text: “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked.
passages.sermon:
Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
Nicodemus spoke to Jesus.
Nicodemus asked Jesus a question.
Nicodemus said, “How can this be?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Νικόδημος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Πῶς δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι

passages.text: “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and you do not understand these things?
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Nicodemus.\r\nJesus said, “You are Israel’s teacher.\r\nYou do not understand these things.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ διδάσκαλος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ταῦτα οὐ γινώσκεις

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and yet you people do not accept our testimony.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nicodemus.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
We speak about things we know.
We tell you what we have seen.
You and your people do not accept our testimony.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ὃ οἴδαμεν λαλοῦμεν καὶ ὃ ἑωράκαμεν μαρτυροῦμεν καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἡμῶν οὐ λαμβάνετε

passages.text: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel.
Jesus said, “I have told you about things on earth.
You do not believe me.
If I tell you about things in heaven, you will not believe me.”
passages.original: Εἰ τὰ ἐπίγεια εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε πῶς ἐὰν εἴπω ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια πιστεύσετε

passages.text: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of Man.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
The Son of Man came down from heaven.
No one else has gone up into heaven.
Only the Son of Man has come down from heaven.
passages.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a leader of Israel.
Moses lifted up a snake in the wilderness.
He did this so the people could look at it and live.
In the same way, the Son of Man must be lifted up.
The Son of Man is Jesus.
God will lift up Jesus.
God will do this so everyone who believes in Jesus will have eternal life.
passages.original: καὶ καθὼς Μωϋσῆς ὕψωσεν τὸν ὄφιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ οὕτως ὑψωθῆναι δεῖ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.
passages.sermon:
God loved the world very much.
God gave His one and only Son.
God did this so that everyone who believes in His Son will not perish.
Everyone who believes in His Son will have eternal life.
passages.original: Οὕτως γὰρ ἠγάπησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν κόσμον ὥστε τὸν Υἱὸν τὸν μονογενῆ ἔδωκεν ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν μὴ ἀπόληται ἀλλ’ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.
passages.sermon: God sent His Son into the world.\r\nGod did not send His Son to condemn the world.\r\nGod sent His Son to save the world through Him.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν Υἱὸν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἵνα κρίνῃ τὸν κόσμον ἀλλ’ ἵνα σωθῇ ὁ κόσμος δι’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.
passages.sermon:
God has one and only Son.
God gave His Son for the world.
Whoever believes in God's Son is not condemned.
Whoever does not believe in God's Son is already condemned.
He is condemned because he has not believed in the name of God's one and only Son.
passages.original: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν οὐ κρίνεται ὁ δὲ μὴ πιστεύων ἤδη κέκριται ὅτι μὴ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ μονογενοῦς Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.
passages.sermon:
God sent His Son, Jesus, into the world.
Jesus is called the Light.
The Light has come into the world.
This is the verdict.
People loved darkness more than the Light.
Their deeds were evil.
That is why they loved darkness instead of the Light.
passages.original: Αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ κρίσις ὅτι τὸ φῶς ἐλήλυθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον καὶ ἠγάπησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι μᾶλλον τὸ σκότος ἢ τὸ φῶς ἦν γὰρ αὐτῶν πονηρὰ τὰ ἔργα

passages.text: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.
passages.sermon:
Everyone who does evil hates the Light.
The Light is Jesus Christ.
People who do evil avoid the Light.
They do not come to the Light.
They fear that the Light will expose their deeds.
They do not want their evil actions to be revealed.
passages.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ φαῦλα πράσσων μισεῖ τὸ φῶς καὶ οὐκ ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸ φῶς ἵνα μὴ ἐλεγχθῇ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.”
passages.sermon: A person who practices the truth comes into the Light.\r\nThis person wants his deeds to be seen clearly.\r\nHis actions show that God has accomplished them.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸ φῶς ἵνα φανερωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ὅτι ἐν Θεῷ ἐστιν εἰργασμένα

passages.text: After this, Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, where He spent some time with them and baptized.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
His disciples followed Him.
After these things happened, Jesus went into the countryside of Judea.
His disciples went with Him.
Jesus stayed there with His disciples.
Jesus baptized people there.
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν γῆν καὶ ἐκεῖ διέτριβεν μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐβάπτιζεν

passages.text: Now John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because the water was plentiful there, and people kept coming to be baptized.
passages.sermon:
John was baptizing people.
He was at Aenon near Salim.
There was plenty of water at that place.
Many people came to John.
He baptized them.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων ἐν Αἰνὼν ἐγγὺς τοῦ Σαλείμ ὅτι ὕδατα πολλὰ ἦν ἐκεῖ καὶ παρεγίνοντο καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο

passages.text: (For John had not yet been thrown into prison.)
passages.sermon:
John was not in prison yet.
People had not arrested John.
John was still free at this time.
This happened before John went to prison.
passages.original: οὔπω γὰρ ἦν βεβλημένος εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν ὁ Ἰωάννης

passages.text: Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and a certain Jew over the issue of ceremonial washing.
passages.sermon:
John had disciples.
A certain Jew spoke with them.
They argued about ceremonial washing.
This dispute happened between John’s disciples and the Jew.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο οὖν ζήτησις ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν Ἰωάννου μετὰ Ἰουδαίου περὶ καθαρισμοῦ

passages.text: So John’s disciples came to him and said, “Look, Rabbi, the One who was with you beyond the Jordan, the One you testified about—He is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him.”
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John had disciples.
John’s disciples came to him.
They spoke to John.
They called him Rabbi.
They said, “Rabbi, there is a man who was with you beyond the Jordan.”
“You testified about this man.”
“Now, this man is baptizing.”
“Everyone is going to him.”
passages.original: καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ῥαββί ὃς ἦν μετὰ σοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ᾧ σὺ μεμαρτύρηκας ἴδε οὗτος βαπτίζει καὶ πάντες ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: John replied, “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.
passages.sermon: John spoke to his disciples.\r\nJohn answered their question.\r\nJohn said, “A person cannot receive anything unless God gives it from heaven.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰωάννης καὶ εἶπεν Οὐ δύναται ἄνθρωπος λαμβάνειν οὐδὲ ἓν ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: You yourselves can testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but am sent ahead of Him.’
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John spoke to his disciples.
John said, “You can testify about my words.”
I told you, ‘I am not the Christ.’
I am not the promised Savior.
God sent me ahead of the Christ.
I came before Him to prepare the way.
passages.original: αὐτοὶ ὑμεῖς μοι μαρτυρεῖτε ὅτι εἶπον ὅτι Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὁ Χριστός ἀλλ’ ὅτι Ἀπεσταλμένος εἰμὶ ἔμπροσθεν ἐκείνου

passages.text: The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom’s voice. That joy is mine, and it is now complete.
passages.sermon:
The bride belongs to the bridegroom.
The bridegroom is the man who has the bride.
The friend of the bridegroom stands nearby.
He listens for the bridegroom’s voice.
He feels great joy when he hears the bridegroom’s voice.
This joy belongs to me now.
My joy is now complete.
passages.original: Ὁ ἔχων τὴν νύμφην νυμφίος ἐστίν ὁ δὲ φίλος τοῦ νυμφίου ὁ ἑστηκὼς καὶ ἀκούων αὐτοῦ χαρᾷ χαίρει διὰ τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ νυμφίου αὕτη οὖν ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ πεπλήρωται

passages.text: He must increase; I must decrease.
passages.sermon: John the Baptist spoke about Jesus Christ.\r\nJohn said, "Jesus must become greater."\r\nJohn said, "I must become less."
passages.original: ἐκεῖνον δεῖ αὐξάνειν ἐμὲ δὲ ἐλαττοῦσθαι

passages.text: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.
passages.sermon:
Jesus comes from above.
Jesus is above all people.
A person from the earth belongs to the earth.
A person from the earth speaks like someone from the earth.
Jesus comes from heaven.
Jesus is above all people.
passages.original: Ὁ ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν ὁ ὢν ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς λαλεῖ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν

passages.text: He testifies to what He has seen and heard, yet no one accepts His testimony.
passages.sermon:
Jesus comes from heaven.
Jesus is above all.
Jesus testifies to what He has seen.
Jesus testifies to what He has heard.
No one accepts His testimony.
passages.original: ὃ ἑώρακεν καὶ ἤκουσεν τοῦτο μαρτυρεῖ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει

passages.text: Whoever accepts His testimony has certified that God is truthful.
passages.sermon: Whoever accepts His testimony certifies something important.\r\nThis person confirms that God is truthful.
passages.original: ὁ λαβὼν αὐτοῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐσφράγισεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἀληθής ἐστιν

passages.text: For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit.
passages.sermon:
God sent a special person.
This person speaks the words of God.
God gives the Spirit to this person.
God does not limit the Spirit He gives.
God gives the Spirit fully.
passages.original: ὃν γὰρ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ Θεοῦ λαλεῖ οὐ γὰρ ἐκ μέτρου δίδωσιν τὸ Πνεῦμα

passages.text: The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father.
Jesus is the Son.
The Father loves the Son.
The Father has given everything to the Son.
All things are in the hands of the Son.
passages.original: Ὁ Πατὴρ ἀγαπᾷ τὸν Υἱόν καὶ πάντα δέδωκεν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever rejects the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.”
passages.sermon:
The Son is Jesus.
God sent Jesus.
Whoever believes in Jesus has eternal life.
Whoever rejects Jesus will not see life.
The wrath of God remains on the person who rejects Jesus.
passages.original: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον ὁ δὲ ἀπειθῶν τῷ Υἱῷ οὐκ ὄψεται ζωήν ἀλλ’ ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ μένει ἐπ’ αὐτόν
